item.title: Mexico Arrests Ex-Governor Over 2014 Student Abduction Case
item.description: Mexican authorities detained a former governor over charges he concealed evidence in the more than decade-old abduction and presumed murder of dozens of students training to be teachers, one of the country’s most infamous criminal cases.

item.title: Yen Surrenders Nearly Half Its Gains from US-Japan Intervention
item.description: The yen is heading into the end of the week having surrendered nearly half of its intervention-driven gains, fueling speculation among traders that authorities may step into the market again.

item.title: Gold Steady as Traders Assess Impact of Hormuz Flare-Up on Rates
item.description: Gold moved in a narrow range as traders assessed the impact of a reported Iranian attack in the Strait of Hormuz on the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.

item.title: Japan’s Households Continue to Cut Spending Despite Wage Gains
item.description: Japan’s household spending unexpectedly fell for a seventh month even as real wages continued to increase, reflecting the impact of persistent inflation on consumer sentiment.

item.title: Atlassian Shares Surge as Revenue Jump Douses AI Fears
item.description: Atlassian Corp. shares surged in after-hours trading after quarterly revenue climbed, easing concerns that the software services company would be overtaken by artificial intelligence applications.

item.title: Chinese Banks Expand Direct Settlement to Aid Yuan’s Global Role
item.description: China is accelerating its push to internationalize the yuan as domestic banks add new foreign currencies available for direct settlement to bypass the dollar in cross-border trade.

item.title: Japan Sees Rush for Covenant Shelter as BBB-Rated Bond Sales Fly
item.description: Japanese companies have already sold more corporate bonds with investor protection this year than in all of 2025, as lower-rated borrowers increasingly turn to the bond market instead of relying solely on bank loans for their funding needs.

item.title: Japan Small Caps Face Survival Race as Topix Cull Looms
item.description: Japan’s Topix stock index is poised for its biggest overhaul, with more than 600 companies — over a third of its constituents — likely to be gradually removed under new eligibility rules, according to analysts’ estimates.

item.title: Oil Gains, Treasuries Hold Losses Before Jobs Data: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil rose as prospects for a lasting agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained elusive. Treasuries held their losses ahead of the key US jobs data report.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
item.description: Oil extended gains after a report that Iran attacked “hostile targets” in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran seeking to bar US ships from the critical waterway in a deal with Oman.

item.title: Fed’s Musalem Calls for Meaningful Restraint on Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem said that with inflation running above the central bank’s 2% target, policymakers cannot afford to tolerate higher inflation while they wait for the possibility of stronger productivity growth.

item.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un Gains $22 Billion Windfall Despite Sanctions
item.description: Trade records and satellite photos show how North Korea's dictator found new cash to fortify his nuclear arsenal.

item.title: Google’s Shakeup Complicates Race With OpenAI, Anthropic
item.description: The tech giant is entering a new period of transition.

item.title: Japan’s Carmakers Forecast Yen Staying Weak Despite US Intervention
item.description: Japan’s carmakers are assuming that the yen will trade near current levels against the US dollar in the coming months, based on forecasts they issued just as the US stepped in to help the Japanese currency from weakening further.

item.title: Kirin Pushes Into Vitamin Sales With $1.4 Billion Jamieson Deal
item.description: Kirin Holdings Co. shares rose 2.4% to near record levels after the Japanese beverage maker announced a deal to acquire Toronto-based Jamieson Wellness Inc. that values the Canadian vitamins and supplements maker at about C$2 billion ($1.4 billion).

item.title: Fed’s Fima Repo Facility Went Unused for 8th Straight Week
item.description: A rarely used Federal Reserve liquidity facility saw no activity last week, suggesting Japan didn’t use the tool in its latest effort to support the yen.

item.title: AIG Profit Beat Estimates, Cites Strong Underwriting
item.description: American International Group Inc. reported second-quarter results that surpassed Wall Street expectations, roughly two months after Eric Andersen took over as chief executive officer.

item.title: Cloudflare Lifts Annual Profit Outlook, Beats Wall Street Target
item.description: Cloudflare Inc. gave a forecast for profit this year that topped Wall Street’s estimates, suggesting that demand for networking services continued to accelerate amid rapid adoption of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Lyft Delivers Bookings Beat With Premium Rides, Misses on Income
item.description: Lyft Inc.’s second-quarter bookings beat expectations, thanks to growing demand for premium rides and strength in European markets, while net income missed estimates.

item.title: Advanced Micro Devices to Buy Startup Taalas for New AI Chips
item.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. is buying Canadian startup Taalas, a move that will let it offer another type of artificial intelligence chip to the burgeoning data center industry.

item.title: Airbnb Lifts 2026 Outlook Again on US, European Demand
item.description: Airbnb Inc. boosted its annual revenue forecast for a second time this year after it saw robust global travel demand, particularly in the US and Europe.

item.title: What Is OpenAI’s Device? A Doughnut-Shaped Speaker That Costs Over $300
item.description: A highly anticipated new device from OpenAI will have a unique look, complete with moving parts that help give it personality, and likely cost more than $300, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Google Grapples With Exit of AI Pioneer and ‘Most Google Person’
item.description: Days after Google unveiled its first Gemini chatbot in 2023 to compete with ChatGPT, Jeff Dean went to an AI conference where he was promptly swarmed by attendees. Suddenly, the Google executive looked at his watch and realized he was due to give a talk minutes later, spurring a rush to take selfies with the influential tech leader before he left.Now, it’s the employees at Google who are bracing for the AI pioneer’s exit. item.title: Why Universal Music Is Struggling to Impress Investors
item.description: In the new AI-era of music, major labels are still scrambling to explain their value

item.title: Banxico Keeps Rate at 6.5%, Signals No Change Going Forward
item.description: Mexico’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate steady while signaling no change at its next meeting, as policymakers weighed slowing inflation and a weakening economy against persistent services inflation and risks from the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Nscale Touts $51 Billion in Contracts, Targets September US IPO
item.description: Nscale is telling prospective investors it has about $51 billion of total contracted revenue ahead of a US initial public offering that could take place as soon as in September, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Mauricio Villamizar Favors More Colombia Interest Rate Hikes
item.description: Investors shouldn’t interpret the Colombian central bank’s decision to pause interest-rate hikes last month as a sign of dovishness, a top policymaker warned.

item.title: IMF’s Katz Sees Bank of Japan Continuing to Normalize Policy
item.description: An economic revival is giving the Bank of Japan room to keep normalizing monetary policy after decades of maintaining an aggressively loose setting, according to the International Monetary Fund’s No. 2 official.

item.title: Colombia Peso Defies Central Bank Bid to Halt Carry-Fueled Rally
item.description: The Colombian peso continues to be the best performing currency in emerging markets as investors shrug off the central bank’s efforts to slow the currency’s rally and instead focus on its carry appeal.

item.title: Warsh’s Faith in Markets Sidelines More Nuanced Fed Policy Tools
item.description: Kevin Warsh’s embrace of financial markets to help the Federal Reserve do its job would mean trading more precise policy tools for a blunt instrument.
